title: Weekly AI Case-Study Deep-Dive: 23 Oct 2026
summary: Five pieces from SPE ATCE 2026 and Gartner: an evaluation harness for Occidental's drilling agent, a multi-agent rig scheduler (+16% projected production gain, -46% rig idle time), a physics-informed RAG agent for offshore gas networks (~90% faster notifications), ADNOC's AI digital twin (1-2% uplift, no extra capex), and Gartner's finding that only 13% of CIOs see significant AI value.

items.title: Building an Evaluation Harness for Oil & Gas AI Agents (Occidental, SPE ATCE 2026)
items.summary: Occidental's DrillingGPT eval (19 SME-curated tasks, each run 5 times) scored pass@5 of 63%, pass@1 of 48% and pass^5 of 37%. The agent can often reach the right answer, but not reliably.

items.title: A Multi-Agent AI Optimization System for Rig Utilization in the Burgan Field (SPE ATCE 2026)
items.summary: Cooperating agents around a genetic algorithm, with human approval kept throughout, projected a 90-day production gain of +16% and cut fleet-average rig idle time 46% versus manual schedules on identical inputs.

items.title: A Physics-Informed, Retrieval-Augmented Industrial Agent for Offshore Gas Networks (SPE ATCE 2026)
items.summary: A governed RAG agent with physical-consistency checks kept humans in operational authority. In eight matched event pairs, notification latency fell about 90% versus the conventional communication path.

items.title: AI-Enabled Digital Twins for Integrated Production Optimization (ADNOC AiPSO, SPE ATCE 2026)
items.summary: Phase 1 across eight producing fields in 2025-2026 gave a sustained 1-2% production uplift with no incremental capex. Autonomy is bounded by real-time engineering operating envelopes.

items.title: Gartner: Only 13% of CIOs Say AI Has Delivered Significant Value (19 Oct 2026)
items.summary: Only 13% of 2,002 CIOs report significant or transformational value. Organizations with rules for stopping pilots are 2.3x more likely to be vanguards, and with rules for retiring low-value production AI 2.6x, yet only 31% and 17% have them.

title: Daily AI Digest: Fri, 23 Oct 2026
summary: The agent stack is getting real infrastructure. Standards moved to a neutral foundation, clouds launched per-agent sandboxes, enterprises showed small fine-tuned models beating frontier ones on cost, and AI-found security bugs are now big enough to take sites offline.

items.title: AI found a critical PHP flaw (PHP2Shell) that puts WordPress, Drupal and Joomla at risk
items.summary: AI-driven bug discovery is speeding up disclosure cycles. The practical lesson is to patch, inventory which runtimes you actually run, and verify running builds. A WAF alone gives false confidence, and that applies to the internal tools your AI apps sit on too.

items.title: Palantir + NVIDIA: small fine-tuned Nemotron models beat frontier models on domain tasks
items.summary: This is the playbook for an industrial company like bp. Take a narrow, high-volume task with lots of labelled history, and a small local model can be cheaper, faster and easier to govern than a frontier API.

items.title: Agent Skills, Open Responses, OpenEnv and OpenSandbox join the Agentic AI Foundation
items.summary: The pieces you'd build an enterprise agent platform on (tools, skills, model APIs, sandboxes) now have vendor-neutral homes. That makes it safer to standardise on them internally. The proposed roadmap includes security guidance for writing and installing skills.

items.title: Microsoft Agent Framework (Python) 1.23 ships breaking MCP 2.x changes
items.summary: MCP 2.x migrations are starting to land in the major frameworks. Pin versions and test tool integrations before you upgrade, and note the secure-by-default push on endpoints and sandbox flags.

items.title: Every agent gets its own computer: Google's Agent Compute Engine, and Modal's sandbox boom
items.summary: Running untrusted agent code safely and cheaply is becoming its own infrastructure layer. Keep credentials outside the sandbox, give each agent its own identity, and stop paying for idle sessions. These are concrete design rules to borrow.

items.title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt runs locally in about 24GB
items.summary: Capable open models that do tool calls and structured output now fit on a single workstation GPU. That makes private prototyping and on-prem pilots cheap to try before you commit to API spend.

items.title: Braintrust live workshop: "Eval foundations: Answering questions about your agent", Wed 4 Nov, 10:00 AM PT (11:30 PM IST)
items.summary: Evals are the skill that separates demos from production. This is a free, concrete framework you can bring back to your team.
